focus.note: Linking words join ideas. Use because for a reason, so for a result, but for a difference, while for two things at once and or for a choice.

focus.note: Albeit, thereby, hence and whereby are formal. Albeit softens a point, thereby shows a result of an action, hence gives a reason and takes a noun, and whereby explains how something works.

speak.title: Role-play: winning back a regular guest
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You run a hotel in an American border town. Your Canadian guests have stopped coming. Phone a regular guest. Offer a deal and ask what would bring them back.

b.text: You stayed at this hotel every winter. This year you went to Mexico. Explain why, listen to the offer, then decide if you will go back.

phrases: We've missed you at the hotel.
I'd like to offer you a special price.
It's not only about the price, to be honest.
We're thinking about trying somewhere new.
What would make you change your mind?
I'll think about it and let you know.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the guest agree to return, and what finally decided it?
